---
title: "Construct a Centered SNP Design Matrix"
---

## Construct a Centered SNP Design Matrix {.unnumbered}


### Description

Build a centered SNP design matrix $W_{ij} = X_{ij} - 2 p_j$ from an
allele-dosage matrix $X$ (entries 0, 1, 2). The output is suitable
for direct use with <code>run_bayesr</code> and
<code>run_bayesa</code>, which are agnostic to whether the design
matrix encodes biallelic SNPs or multi-allelic haplotypes.



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>construct_snp_matrix(X, ref_freq = NULL)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="X">X</code></td>
<td>
Numeric or integer matrix of allele dosages
(typically <code>0</code>, <code>1</code>, or <code>2</code>) with dimensions
<code>n x p_snp</code>. Coerced to <code>double</code> internally.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="ref_freq">ref_freq</code></td>
<td>
Optional numeric vector of length <code>ncol(X)</code>
giving the reference allele frequencies $p_j$ from the training
set. If <code>NULL</code> (default) the frequencies are computed from
<code>X</code> itself (training-set use).
</td></tr>
</table>


### Details

<strong>Training / test workflow.</strong> Always center the test set with
<em>training</em> allele frequencies, never with frequencies recomputed
from the test set itself:


<ol>
<li> Training: call <code>construct_snp_matrix(X_train)</code> (leave
<code>ref_freq = NULL</code>). The returned <code>\$freq</code> contains the
per-SNP reference frequencies $p_j = mean(X_{train,j}) / 2$.

</li>
<li> Test: call <code>construct_snp_matrix(X_test, ref_freq =
    train\$freq)</code> so the columns of <code>W_test</code> are aligned with
<code>W_train</code> on the same baseline frequencies.

</li></ol>

For phased multi-allelic haplotype data, use
<code>construct_wah_matrix</code> instead. For other marker
representations, build the design matrix manually and pass it to the
Bayesian fitters.



### Value

A list with elements:


<dl>
<dt><code>W</code></dt><dd>Numeric matrix <code>n x p_snp</code> of centered dosages
$W_{ij} = X_{ij} - 2 p_j$.
</dd>
<dt><code>freq</code></dt><dd>Numeric vector of length <code>p_snp</code> with the
allele frequencies used for centering.
</dd>
<dt><code>n</code>, <code>p</code></dt><dd>Number of individuals and SNPs.
</dd>
</dl>



### See Also

<code>construct_wah_matrix</code>, <code>run_bayesr</code>,
<code>run_bayesa</code>



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
library("masbayes")

set.seed(1)
n_ind <- 30
n_snp <- 50
maf   <- runif(n_snp, 0.1, 0.5)

# Simulate dosage matrix (0/1/2) for training and test sets
X_train <- matrix(rbinom(n_ind * n_snp, 2, prob = maf),
                  nrow = n_ind)
X_test  <- matrix(rbinom(10    * n_snp, 2, prob = maf),
                  nrow = 10)

# Training: compute frequencies from X_train
train   <- construct_snp_matrix(X_train)
W_train <- train$W

# Test: reuse training frequencies (do NOT recompute from X_test)
test    <- construct_snp_matrix(X_test, ref_freq = train$freq)
W_test  <- test$W

stopifnot(ncol(W_train) == ncol(W_test))

# The returned W can be passed directly to run_bayesr() or run_bayesa()
# together with the response y_train.




```
